predecessors.name: East Francia
predecessors.text: the Transjuran duchy: 'the Central Plateau from the Jura Mountains up to the Great St Bernard Pass', with Geneva, Lausanne, Sion, Aargau, Bern and Valais, Franche-Comté and the estates around…

successors.name: Kingdom of Arles
successors.text: the Kingdom of Burgundy of 933: Upper and Lower Burgundy united under Rudolph II

ledger.x: 888: Rudolph I is elected king of Upper Burgundy at Saint-Maurice.
911: Cliopatria's shape adds two cells near Besançon.
926: the Basel estates and the Aargau edge are added to Upper Burgundy (17 Swiss cells in Cliopatria's 926 shape).
931: Rudolph II receives the Viennois and Lyonnais.
933: Rudolph II takes Provence and unites the Burgundies.
933: Upper Burgundy becomes the Kingdom of Burgundy.
935: the dossier ends where Cliopatria's Upper Burgundy row ends (935) and its Kingdom of Arles begins (936).

wars.name: Rudolph I's Lotharingian war with Arnulf
wars.outcome: Rudolph claims all Lotharingia in 888; Arnulf 'rapidly forced Rudolph to abandon Lotharingia in return for recognition as king of Upper Burgundy'; skirmishing continues intermittently to 894.

wars.name: Rudolph II and Burchard II of Swabia
wars.outcome: Rudolph occupies Basel (916), is defeated by Burchard II at the Battle of Winterthur (919) and makes peace in 922, marrying Burchard's daughter Bertha; the Basel estates come to him in 926 or 935.

wars.name: Rudolph II's Italian campaign
wars.outcome: Invited by Adalbert I of Ivrea, Rudolph defeats Berengar at Fiorenzuola (17 July 923) and is crowned at Pavia; Berengar is murdered in 924; in 926 the Italian nobles turn to Hugh of Arles and Rudolph returns to Upper Burgundy.

wars.name: Rudolph II and Hugh of Italy over Burgundy
wars.outcome: Hugh 'unsuccessfully attempted to take Burgundy from Rudolph's son, Rudolph II', buys him off with the Viennois and Lyonnais (931) and in 933 gives Provence for Rudolph's renunciation of Italy.

certainty.note: The realm is described by regions and estates, not by treaty lines; the Swabian frontier at Basel and the Italian conquest of 923-926 are approximate.
